chunks: Ibrāhīm al-Karkhī narrated from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, from his forefathers عليهم السلام, who said: al-Ḥasan ibn ʿAlī عليه السلام said:

Regarding the dining table, there are twelve qualities which every Muslim must know: four of them are obligatory, four are sunnah (recommended practices), and four are manners. As for the obligatory ones, they are: recognition, contentment, naming Allah, and gratitude. As for the sunnah, they are: wudu (ablution) before food, sitting on the left side, eating with three fingers, and licking the fingers. As for the manners, they are: eating from what is nearest to you, making the morsel small, chewing well, and minimizing looking at people's faces.

key_terms.التَّسْمِيَةُ: mentioning the name of Allah before eating
key_terms.الشُّكْرُ: gratitude to Allah for the provision
key_terms.الْمَائِدَةِ: the dining table or meal setting
key_terms.تَأْدِيبٌ: refined etiquette and discipline in conduct
key_terms.فَرْضٌ: an obligatory duty in this context

ai.seo_question: What are the Islamic etiquettes and sunnah practices of eating according to Imam al-Hasan عليه السلام?
ai.summary: This hadith organizes the etiquettes of eating into three categories: obligations, sunnah practices, and refined manners. It shows that dining in Islam is not merely a physical act, but one connected to ma'rifah, gratitude, ritual purity, and consideration for others.
